lands 2 or 3 of them on each SIMD depending on whether it is spread over
the WGP's four SIMDs or its CU's two. Either way the matrix pipe on a SIMD
has at most two other waves to run while one waits on a load. Both head-128
attentions spill more than 100 registers to scratch.

## The energy roofline (2026-09-29, §0.7)

The GEMM ladder at N = 2048 drew **136–137 W at every rung from 23 to 39
TFLOP/s**; the winner won by needing less energy a FLOP under the same
cap. So the roofline that binds a real kernel on this part is joules,
not clocks, and it is already in `results/*.csv` (the `power_w` column):

| what | rate | PPT | energy | above ~20 W idle |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| matrix pipe, registers only, 16 chains (`peak`) | 55.5 TFLOP/s | 98 W | **567 GFLOP/J** | 1.4 pJ a FLOP |
| the same at 4 chains (the old probe) | 55.5 | 112 W | 495 | +14 W of loop issue |
| `dot4_int8` / packed fp16 FMA / fp32 FMA | 54 / 25 / 23 T | 118–121 W | 450 / 215 / 189 | |
| MALL-resident copy (1–4 MB) | 800 GB/s | 105–136 W | 6–8 GB/J | ~100 pJ a byte |
| DRAM stream (≥ 6 MB) | 236 GB/s | 136 W | **1.7 GB/J** | **~490 pJ a byte** |
| best suite GEMM | 39.0 TFLOP/s | 137 W | 285 GFLOP/J | |
| a video forward, every kernel | 32.5 TFLOP/s | 149 W | 218 GFLOP/J | |
| LLM prefill, 8,192 tokens, 24 of 48 layers (`cmd/llm -graph`) | 2,680 tok/s (≈1,340 at 48) | **142 W** at 2713 MHz | ≈ 110 mJ a token at 48 layers | |
| LLM decode, 24 of 48 layers (`cmd/llm -gen`) | 63.2 tok/s (≈31.6 at 48) | **91 W** at 2590 MHz | ≈ 2.9 J a token at 48 layers | memory-bound: the bytes, not the clock |

A DRAM byte costs the energy of ~340 matrix FLOPs, a MALL byte ~70.
The matrix cores at full rate are ~80 W over idle, so **at a 150 W cap a
real GEMM has ~50 W for everything else** (bytes at every level, address
arithmetic, issue), which is 100 GB/s of DRAM-priced traffic or ~500 GB/s
of MALL-priced: a kernel at 55 TFLOP/s and AI 43 moves 1.3 TB/s through
the L0/L1, and whether that fits depends on the pJ a byte at *those*
levels, which are not measured (G0b). This is also why a
register-resident loop "reaches peak at ~90 W" wherever it is claimed:
that is the probe, and the other 50–70 W in a real kernel is bytes.

**An outside calibration** (2026-09-29): `peonist-ai/halogen-flash-server`
claims, for the same model on the same part, prefill at 1,567–1,584 tok/s
(8k–32k prompts) and 1,517 at 131k, serial decode 37.6 tok/s at 1.5k and
34.1 at 32k, and 46–56 tok/s with a draft head plus prompt lookup, at
"about 85 W of sustained package power" and a 2,229 MHz median clock
during a 32k prefill. Against ours: prefill 1,213 at 8k and 1,011–1,022
at 128k (1.25–1.5x behind) at 142 W (so ~2x the energy a token); serial
decode 34.4 at depth 0 and 31.5 at 128k (within 10%) at 91 W (about
the same joules a token as their 108–118 W would give); our speculative
loop is parked at 0.95x where theirs is 1.35–1.5x. The repository is
documentation and a container image, not source ("Shell", no kernel
files), so the how is not inspectable. The image was not run here, on
purpose: the hardware is the same part under the same ~150 W cap, so
their 85 W at 2229 MHz is what their prefill *draws*, not a limit it
runs under, and the comparison needs no more than the two power
readings. The prefill gap is the one this vertical can act on: a 2x in
joules a token at a *lower* clock says their prefill moves far fewer
bytes a token through the memory system than ours, which is G5's
territory (4-bit weights straight into the matrix cores without the LDS
round trip) and G6's (the streaming kernels between the GEMMs).

What it changes: an arm that hides latency without moving fewer bytes
(a register prefetch) buys the in-wave stall and no clock; an arm that
moves fewer bytes a FLOP (LDS sharing across a workgroup's waves, bigger
effective tiles, fewer wasted instructions) buys twice. G2's order below
is set by that.

## Why 76% and not 90%: the hypotheses, each with its measurement

Every GEMM lever in the tree so far changed *what* is loaded (intensity,
stride, layout, order). None changed *when*, except §2.7, which changed only
the scheduling and was worth 2.1x. The remaining gap is most likely
scheduling again.

- **H1 — the clock.** 3% is already measured (2813 against 2899). Whether
  a sustained kernel loses more is §6.4, never run. *Measure*: sysmon over
  a 60 s GEMM loop and over one H3 forward, CPU idle and CPU busy (the
  server tokenises and decodes audio beside the device). Cheap, and it
  fixes the denominator for everything below.
- **H2 — latency exposed at the K-tile boundary.** The shipped loop is
  `BK_TILES 1`, no hoist: per K tile a wave issues 4 A + 8 B fragment loads
  and 32 MMAs, then the next tile's loads. 32 wave64 MMAs are ~1,100 clocks
  of matrix-pipe time (8,192 FLOP each at 239 FLOP/clk/SIMD); a fragment
  load from L2 or the MALL is several hundred to ~2,000 clocks. Unless the
  compiler already issues tile k+1's loads before tile k's MMAs, each wave
  stalls once a tile, and with 2–3 waves a SIMD the pipe idles part of the
  time. A 20–25% shortfall is exactly the size of one exposed latency per
  tile at this occupancy. *Measure*: G1 reads the ISA (where the
  `s_waitcnt` sits relative to the `v_wmma` block), then G2 builds the
  register-prefetch arm: tile k+1's 12 fragments loaded into a second
  register set before tile k's MMAs issue. That is +24 VGPRs; at WN = 8 it
  is 264 and spills, so the arm is WM 4 × WN 4 (16 accumulators, 64 VGPRs)
  in a 4-wave 128×128 workgroup, or WM 8 × WN 4, and the AI drop (43 → 32)
  is part of what is measured. **This is the lever the plan is built
  around.** *G2's answer (§2.9): the latency is the cost, but a fragment
  is 8 VGPRs (4x replicated at wave64), ACO copies any fragment carried
  across the loop's back-edge element by element, and the prefetch that
  fits is a whole slab through LDS at wave32: 74 → 80% per clock.*
- **H3 — the issue budget.** A wave64 MMA holds the matrix pipe ~34 clocks;
  if the loop spends more than ~30 VALU/SALU issue slots per MMA on
  address arithmetic, waitcnts and loads, the SIMD is issue-bound, not
  latency-bound. *Measure*: instruction count per K tile from the ISA
  (§2.3's route: the B-layout finding was an instruction count). If it is
  under ~8 non-MMA instructions an MMA, this is not it.
- **H4 — the epilogue.** 32 fp32 tiles a wave stored row-major with no
  overlap inside the wave: 63 MB of C at M = 4096 × N = 3840, 0.27 ms at
  the bus, of a 2.9 ms GEMM. **~9% if nothing overlaps it**, and other
  workgroups' MMAs only overlap it if a second workgroup fits on the CU.
  *Measure*: the `C_F16` build (halves it; already exists, allowed where
  the consumer narrows anyway) against the fp32 store, and a control that
  stores one tile of the 32 (the compiler must not be allowed to drop the
  MMAs: keep the store conditional on a push constant).
- **H5 — the grid tail.** 480 workgroups of 128×256 at the DiT's shape, one
  or two resident a CU, so 6–12 rounds; a shape whose last round is a
  quarter full loses up to a round. *Measure*: rate against M in steps of
  128 rows on one N, K; the tail's size falls out of the sawtooth.
- **H6 — L0/L1 traffic.** At 42 TFLOP/s and AI 43 the fragment loads move
  ~1 TB/s, above the MALL's 965 GB/s pure read, so the L0/L1 hit rate is
  carrying the kernel. The two waves of a workgroup that share an A slab
  each load it. LDS staging lost in §2.1 at AI 8–32 on an unhoisted,
  untiled kernel; it has not been asked at the current tiling. *Measure*:
  only after G2, and only if the prefetch arm lands short of 85%: one LDS
  arm on the *tiled* B (a slab is 512 B contiguous tiles, so the staging
  is a copy, not a gather). *G2: built, and it is the shipped kernel;
  with the staging loads made L0 hits the build reaches 82%, so the memory
  system is now ~3 points and the LDS-side schedule ~18 (G-o8).*
- **H7 — the accumulator chain.** 32 independent accumulators a K tile;
  the MMA latency is hidden. Not it; listed so no one re-tests it.

**Attention** (68–70%, and both shipped head-128 builds spill 112–126):

- **A1 — the spill.** `T QT2 KTIL4` spills 112 and wins; `T QT2 KTIL2` is
  spill-free at 256 and loses 15%; reloading Q each block removes the
  spill and loses 11%. Untried: **a head-dimension split** (two passes of
  64 channels; the head-64 build is spill-free at 240 and runs 34
  TFLOP/s on the VAE), and **wave64** for the transposed kernel (its
  element order is wave32's; the probe says what wave64's is, and at wave64
  the same tile needs half the VGPRs per fragment). *Measure*: the existing
  screen (`TestGPUAttentionScreen`, `H3_ATTN_SPV=qt:ktil:path`).
- **A2 — the online rescale.** Every key block rescales the 8 O^T
  accumulator tiles of a query tile, 8 elements a lane each, plus the
  running sum, whether or not the row max moved. FlashAttention-3's lazy
  rescaling skips it while the max grows by less than a threshold and
  corrects once at the end; exact up to fp32 rounding order. *Measure*:
  the screen, and rms against the plain kernel ≤ 1.1e-4 as M11c gated.
- **A3 — an honest gutting.** M11c's "no LDS round trip" arm read 65.7
  TFLOP/s, above the ceiling, so the compiler dropped MMAs and that arm is
  not a measurement. *Redo*: each phase removed with its result kept live
  (folded into the stored O), so the MMA-only floor of the transposed loop
  is a real number. If it is ~40, the softmax is not the cost and A1 is
  the whole story; if 45+, A2 is worth up to 15%.

**Int8 and Q4 weights** (the LLM's prefill, Kev, embeddings, video's
dequant pass): **G5** builds the B fragment in registers from the bytes
the lane loads itself, using the element order the probe pins (A: lane l
holds row l%16, element e is column e; B: lane l holds column l%16,
element e is row e). No LDS, no barrier, and the plain path stays as the
fallback the probe selects. The MoE Q4 GEMM's 51% is the first customer;
the LLM's prefill graph runs at 9.8 TFLOP/s of useful work (P11), most of
it on these kernels.

## Decisions (so future sessions don't relitigate)

1. **The ceiling is per clock, and the clock is set by energy.** A
   kernel's utilisation is FLOP/clk/CU against the probe's 480, at the
   clock sysmon saw *during that kernel*. Every timing this vertical
   records carries its sclk and package power (PPT), and every kernel
   table carries **GFLOP/J** (or GB/J) beside its rate. The package is
   capped near 150 W (§0.6), so rate = cap ÷ energy per operation: a
   kernel that spends fewer joules a FLOP runs at a higher clock and is
   faster for that reason alone. Power efficiency is not a second
   objective here; it is the same one (§0.7).
2. **The suite is the ablation instrument; the vertical kernels are where
   a winner ships.** `gemm_wmma.comp` + `results/gemm_wmma.csv` stay a
   measured artifact of a kernel that does not move under them (the
   header in `dit_gemm.comp` says why). A lever is proved in the suite on
   the `shapes` family (the models' real M, N, K), then ported to
   `dit_gemm.comp` as a `-D` and screened in the verticals with their own
   tools: `TestGPUShapes`/`H3_PROFILE` (video), the zimage DiT ladder
   (image), `cmd/kevload`, the LLM prefill bench.
3. **Bit-identical or the vertical's own gate.** A scheduling change
   (prefetch, tile order, epilogue store) makes the same MMAs in the same
   order and must be byte-identical (`TestGPUForward` asserts it, as
   M11d's split did). A numeric change (lazy rescale, fp16 C) goes through
   the consumer's gate (rms ≤ 1.1e-4 on a context; the teacher-forced step
   bounds), never a max-abs on a free run.
4. **Read the ISA before building the arm.** `cmd/probe` is back; a
   hypothesis about scheduling or issue is checked in the disassembly
   first, because §2.3 and §6.1 showed that is where the answers were.
5. **Wave size and element order are per kernel, probed, with a plain
   fallback.** Nothing written against a lane layout ships without
   `checkCoopMatLayout`'s equivalent selecting it at first use.
6. **A finding is filed under the next free `§N.M`** (§2.9 the prefetch,
   §3.8 the attention rescale, §2.10 the register dequant …) with its
   file in `research/`, and the G-stage here points at it. Numbers are
   never reused.
7. **Stop when three consecutive well-formed hypotheses move nothing by
   2%.** The exit is a measured plateau, not a percentage: 85% is the
   target, not the gate.

## The stages

| # | Stage | State |
|---|---|---|
| G0 | Instruments: `cmd/probe` restored; the `peak` probe at wave32 and at 16 chains (is 478/clk the hardware or the probe?); sysmon around every in-pipeline timing this vertical takes; §6.4's sustained-clock run (H1) | **done 2026-09-29** (§0.6): the ceiling is the hardware's, 478–482 FLOP/clk/CU at every chain count and wave size; **a video forward runs at 2600–2650 MHz and ~149 W**, so its ceiling is 49.9 TFLOP/s and the shipped GEMM is at 74% of it; 32 busy CPU threads take the GPU to 1350 MHz and a forward to 1.67x |
| G0b | The energy roofline: pJ a byte at L0, L1, L2, MALL and DRAM (the `bandwidth` family below its 2 MB floor, with the power column), pJ a FLOP per instruction class (done, §0.7), the sensor settled (PPT is the package; the CPU's share from the RAPL counter in `/sys/class/powercap`, GPU = PPT − CPU), and GFLOP/J in every profile this vertical prints | **§0.7 opened 2026-09-29** from the recorded rows; the cache levels and the sensor split are open |
| G1 | The shipped GEMM's ISA: one K iteration's schedule (loads, waitcnts, MMAs), instructions per MMA, occupancy as the driver places it (H2, H3) | **done 2026-09-29** (§6.5): no prefetch across K tiles, 85 address instructions recomputed an iteration; **the rate is flat from 1 to 3+ workgroups a CU**; with every load an L0 hit the GEMMs reach 82–85% per clock, so the memory system is ~10 points and the in-wave schedule ~16 |
| G2 | The register-prefetch GEMM (H2): `PREFETCH=1` in `gemm_wmma.comp` and `dit_gemm.comp`, the tile geometries it fits in, screened on the `shapes` family and on the DiT's and H3's shapes; bit-identical | **done 2026-09-29** (§2.9): not registers, **LDS**: the K slab staged a slab ahead through 24 staging registers into a double-buffered LDS plane, at **wave32** (a fragment is 8 VGPRs and 4x its bytes at wave64, 2x at wave32), 4×4 tiles, eight waves. Bit-identical; H3's projections **37 → 41 TFLOP/s**, the split down projection **29 → 41**, a 480p forward **29.9 → 27.1 s**; 74 → 80% per clock. Shipped for H3; the other eight hosts are G8 |
| G3 | The epilogue and the tail (H4, H5): the store's cost priced with a live control; `C_F16` and the fragment-tile C for attention's operands (stage 4's open item) where the consumer allows; the M sawtooth | |
| G4 | Attention (A1–A3): the honest gutting first, then a head-split and a wave64 transposed build, then lazy rescaling; every build through the H3 screen and the image DiT's; carried to the VAE, Kev, OCR, ACE (every `dit_attention_wmma.comp` user still pays the LDS round trip M11c removed) | |
| G5 | Int8/Q4 B fragments built in registers from the probed layout: the MoE Q4 GEMM (51% → ?), `llm_gemm`'s Q8 arm, `kev_gemm_q8_glu`, and H3's dequant pass folded away | |
| G6 | The streaming kernels: a bandwidth column in every vertical's profile, the ones under 200 GB/s listed and fixed or fused (`hc.cn` at 134 first) | |
| G7 | The budget: what the server's CPU work beside a device job costs in GPU clock (the audio decode's 32 threads, staging on 32 cores, tokenising; G0 measured 32 busy threads at 1.67x), whether a thread cap or a CPU power limit is a net win, and the sampler folded into `bench/sysmon.go` around the vertical tests | G0 measured the extremes; the server's own load is open |
| G8 | Carry-in: each vertical's screen re-run on the new builds, the numbers into VIDEO.md M11, the image and LLM records, and TODO.md's table | continuous. **G2 carried to all nine hosts 2026-09-29** (table below): every gate passes; the image step 2179 → 2058 ms, the VAE decode 37.1 → 35.5 s, Kev's fp16 pass at 494 tokens 154 → 132 ms; **the build loses below ~1000 rows** (a 30-workgroup grid), so `ace/dit` keeps the wave64 build up to 1024 rows and the ladders' schedules already keep it off short inputs |

**Order:** G0 (a day: it fixes the denominator), G1 (a session: it decides
between H2 and H3 before anything is built), G2 (the big one), then G4 and
G5 in either order, G3 and G6 as the profiles point, G7 when a long run is
happening anyway, G8 after every win.

**Gates, per stage:** G0 a ceiling table reproduced twice with clocks. G1 a
written schedule of one K iteration from the disassembly, with the
instruction counts. G2 the suite's best and `dit.qkv`'s rate, two runs
each, bit-identical C, and the register/spill line from `cmd/probe`. G3
the priced store and the sawtooth, both with clocks. G4 the H3 screen
table and rms against the plain kernel, plus `TestGPUForward`/`TestGPURun`
unchanged. G5 bit-identical to the LDS path on the MoE bench, and the
prefill rate. G6 a table of every streaming kernel over 1 ms in a block
with its GB/s. G7 the trace.

### G0 — instruments and the ceiling (2026-09-29)

Filed as **§0.6** in `research/0-measurement-validity.md`.

**The ceiling is the hardware's.** The `peak` family gained the WMMA loop
at 8 and 16 chains and at wave32 (`-DACC`, `-DWAVE`; `bench/ops_peak.go`
pins the size), so G-o1 could be answered instead of assumed:

| probe | best | sclk | W | FLOP/clk/CU |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| wmma_fp16, 4 chains, wave64 (the old probe) | 55,554 | 2890 | 112 | 481 |
| 8 chains | 55,615 | 2890 | 99 | 481 |
| 16 chains | 55,524 | 2890 | 98 | 480 |
| wave32, 4 chains | 55,436 | 2892 | 98 | 479 |
| wave32, 8 chains | 55,405 | 2896 | 100 | 478 |
| wmma_int8 | 55,538 | 2879 | 98 | 482 |

Flat to 1% across all of them, at **480 of the spec's 512**, which is
15/16 exactly: the matrix pipe's dense rate on this silicon, not a probe
artefact. 55.5 TFLOP/s at 2899 MHz stands, and every rate below is read
against 480 FLOP/clk/CU at the clock the kernel ran at.

**The clock under a real kernel.** A 100 ms sampler on
`hwmon/freq1_input` and `power1_average` around `TestGPUShapes`
(`H3_SHAPES=1 H3_PROFILE=1`, int8, the machine otherwise idle):

| what | sclk (mode) | package W | a 480p forward | a 768p forward |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `peak` probe | 2890–2899 | 100–112 | | |
| suite GEMM, 20 ms bursts (`results/gemm_wmma.csv`) | 2813 | 137 | | |
| **H3 forward, CPU idle** | **2600–2650** | **149** | 30.0 s | |
| H3 768p forward, CPU idle (sustained ~2 min) | 2550–2600 | 142–155 | | 106.7 s |
| **H3 forward, 32 busy CPU threads** | **1300–1400** | 121 (GPU side) | **50.1 s** | **190 s** |

Three things. **The package is power-limited at ~150 W**, and a GEMM's
memory traffic costs ~40 W over the register-only probe, so the clock
sags 9–10% under any real kernel: the ceiling during a video forward is
**49.9 TFLOP/s**, not 55.5, and the shipped GEMM's 37 TFLOP/s there is
**74% per clock** (353 FLOP/clk/CU), the attention's 37.3 is 75%, the
whole forward's 32.5 is 65%. **The 768p run sags further** (2550–2600),
so long forwards are ~2% slower per FLOP than short ones for the clock
alone. And **the CPU shares the budget**: 32 busy host threads halve the
GPU clock and make a forward 1.67x slower. That is the mechanism behind
VIDEO.md M11f's "+2.4 s of device time while the audio decodes on 32
threads": not memory contention, the power budget. Anything the server
runs on the CPU beside a device job costs GPU clock in proportion to its
power, which is a serving rule this repo did not have.

**Instruments.** `cmd/probe` is back (`RADV_DEBUG=shaderstats|asm`),
`H3_GEMM_SPV=path` runs a big-GEMM build from disk in `TestGPUShapes`
(and times it even when it is wrong by construction), and the sampler
is `scratchpad/sample.sh`-shaped: 100 ms of `freq1_input`,
`power1_average`; a phase is the samples between two timestamps. It is
not in the tree yet; G7 should fold it into `bench/sysmon.go` around the
vertical tests.

### G1 — the shipped GEMM's schedule (2026-09-29)

Filed as **§6.5** in `research/6.5-gemm-schedule.md`.

**The loop, from the disassembly** (`dit_gemm_wg128x256_bt16_swz8`,
wave64, 240 VGPRs, no spill, no LDS; ACO says 6 subgroups a SIMD, which
is not the arithmetic of a 1536-register file at wave64 and is not
relied on). One iteration is one 16-wide K tile:

| instructions | count | what |
|---|---|---|
| `v_wmma_f32_16x16x16_f16` | 32 | the 4×8 accumulator grid |
| `buffer_load_b128` | 24 | 4 A + 8 B fragments, 2 loads each, in 3 clauses |
| `s_add/s_mul/s_lshr/s_lshl/s_load/s_mov` | 56 | the B tile addresses, **recomputed every iteration** |
| `v_lshlrev/v_add3/v_mul_lo/v_mbcnt/v_and` | 29 | the A addresses and lane offset, likewise |
| `s_delay_alu` | 20 | dependency stalls in that arithmetic |
| `s_waitcnt` | 9 | `vmcnt(14)`, then 12, 10, … 0, four MMAs between each |
| `s_clause`, branch, compare | 5 | |

Order: address arithmetic → all 24 loads → `s_waitcnt vmcnt(14)` (A and
the first B landed) → 4 MMAs → wait → 4 MMAs … → `vmcnt(0)` → the last 4
→ loop. **G-o3 answered: no.** ACO does not hoist the next tile's loads
above this tile's MMAs; each iteration pays the load latency once, from
the address arithmetic to the tenth lo

20	480p video forward is 63% GEMM and 33% attention on these kernels, an
21	image step 72% GEMM, a prefill chunk mostly GEMM. **A 1.15x on the GEMM is

141	
142	The GEMM ladder at N = 2048 drew **136–137 W at every rung from 23 to 39
143	TFLOP/s**; the winner won by needing less energy a FLOP under the same
144	cap. So the roofline that binds a real kernel on this part is joules,
145	not clocks, and it is already in `results/*.csv` (the `power_w` column):
146	
147	| what | rate | PPT | energy | above ~20 W idle |
148	|---|---|---|---|---|
149	| matrix pipe, registers only, 16 chains (`peak`) | 55.5 TFLOP/s | 98 W | **567 GFLOP/J** | 1.4 pJ a FLOP |
150	| the same at 4 chains (the old probe) | 55.5 | 112 W | 495 | +14 W of loop issue |
151	| `dot4_int8` / packed fp16 FMA / fp32 FMA | 54 / 25 / 23 T | 118–121 W | 450 / 215 / 189 | |
152	| MALL-resident copy (1–4 MB) | 800 GB/s | 105–136 W | 6–8 GB/J | ~100 pJ a byte |
153	| DRAM stream (≥ 6 MB) | 236 GB/s | 136 W | **1.7 GB/J** | **~490 pJ a byte** |
154	| best suite GEMM | 39.0 TFLOP/s | 137 W | 285 GFLOP/J | |
155	| a video forward, every kernel | 32.5 TFLOP/s | 149 W | 218 GFLOP/J | |
156	| LLM prefill, 8,192 tokens, 24 of 48 layers (`cmd/llm -graph`) | 2,680 tok/s (≈1,340 at 48) | **142 W** at 2713 MHz | ≈ 110 mJ a token at 48 layers | |
157	| LLM decode, 24 of 48 layers (`cmd/llm -gen`) | 63.2 tok/s (≈31.6 at 48) | **91 W** at 2590 MHz | ≈ 2.9 J a token at 48 layers | memory-bound: the bytes, not the clock |
158	
159	A DRAM byte costs the energy of ~340 matrix FLOPs, a MALL byte ~70.
160	The matrix cores at full rate are ~80 W over idle, so **at a 150 W cap a
161	real GEMM has ~50 W for everything else** (bytes at every level, address
162	arithmetic, issue), which is 100 GB/s of DRAM-priced traffic or ~500 GB/s
163	of MALL-priced: a kernel at 55 TFLOP/s and AI 43 moves 1.3 TB/s through
164	the L0/L1, and whether that fits depends on the pJ a byte at *those*
165	levels, which are not measured (G0b). This is also why a
166	register-resident loop "reaches peak at ~90 W" wherever it is claimed:
167	that is the probe, and the other 50–70 W in a real kernel is bytes.
168	
169	**An outside calibration** (2026-09-29): `peonist-ai/halogen-flash-server`
170	claims, for the same model on the same part, prefill at 1,567–1,584 tok/s
171	(8k–32k prompts) and 1,517 at 131k, serial decode 37.6 tok/s at 1.5k and
172	34.1 at 32k, and 46–56 tok/s with a draft head plus prompt lookup, at
173	"about 85 W of sustained package power" and a 2,229 MHz median clock
174	during a 32k prefill. Against ours: prefill 1,213 at 8k and 1,011–1,022
175	at 128k (1.25–1.5x behind) at 142 W (so ~2x the energy a token); serial
176	decode 34.4 at depth 0 and 31.5 at 128k (within 10%) at 91 W (about
177	the same joules a token as their 108–118 W would give); our speculative
178	loop is parked at 0.95x where theirs is 1.35–1.5x. The repository is
179	documentation and a container image, not source ("Shell", no kernel
180	files), so the how is not inspectable. The image was not run here, on
181	purpose: the hardware is the same part under the same ~150 W cap, so
182	their 85 W at 2229 MHz is what their prefill *draws*, not a limit it
183	runs under, and the comparison needs no more than the two power
184	readings. The prefill gap is the one this vertical can act on: a 2x in
185	joules a token at a *lower* clock says their prefill moves far fewer
186	bytes a token through the memory system than ours, which is G5's
187	territory (4-bit weights straight into the matrix cores without the LDS
188	round trip) and G6's (the streaming kernels between the GEMMs).
189	
190	What it changes: an arm that hides latency without moving fewer bytes
191	(a register prefetch) buys the in-wave stall and no clock; an arm that
192	moves fewer bytes a FLOP (LDS sharing across a workgroup's waves, bigger
193	effective tiles, fewer wasted instructions) buys twice. G2's order below
194	is set by that.

196	## Why 76% and not 90%: the hypotheses, each with its measurement
197	
198	Every GEMM lever in the tree so far changed *what* is loaded (intensity,
199	stride, layout, order). None changed *when*, except §2.7, which changed only
200	the scheduling and was worth 2.1x. The remaining gap is most likely
201	scheduling again.
202	
203	- **H1 — the clock.** 3% is already measured (2813 against 2899). Whether
204	  a sustained kernel loses more is §6.4, never run. *Measure*: sysmon over
205	  a 60 s GEMM loop and over one H3 forward, CPU idle and CPU busy (the
206	  server tokenises and decodes audio beside the device). Cheap, and it
207	  fixes the denominator for everything below.
208	- **H2 — latency exposed at the K-tile boundary.** The shipped loop is
209	  `BK_TILES 1`, no hoist: per K tile a wave issues 4 A + 8 B fragment loads
210	  and 32 MMAs, then the next tile's loads. 32 wave64 MMAs are ~1,100 clocks
211	  of matrix-pipe time (8,192 FLOP each at 239 FLOP/clk/SIMD); a fragment
212	  load from L2 or the MALL is several hundred to ~2,000 clocks. Unless the
213	  compiler already issues tile k+1's loads before tile k's MMAs, each wave
214	  stalls once a tile, and with 2–3 waves a SIMD the pipe idles part of the
215	  time. A 20–25% shortfall is exactly the size of one exposed latency per
216	  tile at this occupancy. *Measure*: G1 reads the ISA (where the
217	  `s_waitcnt` sits relative to the `v_wmma` block), then G2 builds the
218	  register-prefetch arm: tile k+1's 12 fragments loaded into a second
219	  register set before tile k's MMAs issue. That is +24 VGPRs; at WN = 8 it
220	  is 264 and spills, so the arm is WM 4 × WN 4 (16 accumulators, 64 VGPRs)
221	  in a 4-wave 128×128 workgroup, or WM 8 × WN 4, and the AI drop (43 → 32)
222	  is part of what is measured. **This is the lever the plan is built
223	  around.** *G2's answer (§2.9): the latency is the cost, but a fragment
224	  is 8 VGPRs (4x replicated at wave64), ACO copies any fragment carried
225	  across the loop's back-edge element by element, and the prefetch that
226	  fits is a whole slab through LDS at wave32: 74 → 80% per clock.*
227	- **H3 — the issue budget.** A wave64 MMA holds the matrix pipe ~34 clocks;
228	  if the loop spends more than ~30 VALU/SALU issue slots per MMA on
229	  address arithmetic, waitcnts and loads, the SIMD is issue-bound, not
230	  latency-bound. *Measure*: instruction count per K tile from the ISA
231	  (§2.3's route: the B-layout finding was an instruction count). If it is
232	  under ~8 non-MMA instructions an MMA, this is not it.
233	- **H4 — the epilogue.** 32 fp32 tiles a wave stored row-major with no
234	  overlap inside the wave: 63 MB of C at M = 4096 × N = 3840, 0.27 ms at
235	  the bus, of a 2.9 ms GEMM. **~9% if nothing overlaps it**, and other
236	  workgroups' MMAs only overlap it if a second workgroup fits on the CU.
237	  *Measure*: the `C_F16` build (halves it; already exists, allowed where
238	  the consumer narrows anyway) against the fp32 store, and a control that
239	  stores one tile of the 32 (the compiler must not be allowed to drop the
240	  MMAs: keep the store conditional on a push constant).
241	- **H5 — the grid tail.** 480 workgroups of 128×256 at the DiT's shape, one
242	  or two resident a CU, so 6–12 rounds; a shape whose last round is a
243	  quarter full loses up to a round. *Measure*: rate against M in steps of
244	  128 rows on one N, K; the tail's size falls out of the sawtooth.
245	- **H6 — L0/L1 traffic.** At 42 TFLOP/s and AI 43 the fragment loads move
246	  ~1 TB/s, above the MALL's 965 GB/s pure read, so the L0/L1 hit rate is
247	  carrying the kernel. The two waves of a workgroup that share an A slab
248	  each load it. LDS staging lost in §2.1 at AI 8–32 on an unhoisted,
249	  untiled kernel; it has not been asked at the current tiling. *Measure*:
250	  only after G2, and only if the prefetch arm lands short of 85%: one LDS
251	  arm on the *tiled* B (a slab is 512 B contiguous tiles, so the staging
252	  is a copy, not a gather). *G2: built, and it is the shipped kernel;
253	  with the staging loads made L0 hits the build reaches 82%, so the memory
254	  system is now ~3 points and the LDS-side schedule ~18 (G-o8).*
255	- **H7 — the accumulator chain.** 32 independent accumulators a K tile;
256	  the MMA latency is hidden. Not it; listed so no one re-tests it.
257	
258	**Attention** (68–70%, and both shipped head-128 builds spill 112–126):
259	
260	- **A1 — the spill.** `T QT2 KTIL4` spills 112 and wins; `T QT2 KTIL2` is
261	  spill-free at 256 and loses 15%; reloading Q each block removes the
262	  spill and loses 11%. Untried: **a head-dimension split** (two passes of
263	  64 channels; the head-64 build is spill-free at 240 and runs 34
264	  TFLOP/s on the VAE), and **wave64** for the transposed kernel (its
265	  element order is wave32's; the probe says what wave64's is, and at wave64
266	  the same tile needs half the VGPRs per fragment). *Measure*: the existing
267	  screen (`TestGPUAttentionScreen`, `H3_ATTN_SPV=qt:ktil:path`).
268	- **A2 — the online rescale.** Every key block rescales the 8 O^T
269	  accumulator tiles of a query tile, 8 elements a lane each, plus the
270	  running sum, whether or not the row max moved. FlashAttention-3's lazy
271	  rescaling skips it while the max grows by less than a threshold and
272	  corrects once at the end; exact up to fp32 rounding order. *Measure*:
273	  the screen, and rms against the plain kernel ≤ 1.1e-4 as M11c gated.
274	- **A3 — an honest gutting.** M11c's "no LDS round trip" arm read 65.7
275	  TFLOP/s, above the ceiling, so the compiler dropped MMAs and that arm is
276	  not a measurement. *Redo*: each phase removed with its result kept live
277	  (folded into the stored O), so the MMA-only floor of the transposed loop
278	  is a real number. If it is ~40, the softmax is not the cost and A1 is
279	  the whole story; if 45+, A2 is worth up to 15%.

281	**Int8 and Q4 weights** (the LLM's prefill, Kev, embeddings, video's
282	dequant pass): **G5** builds the B fragment in registers from the bytes
283	the lane loads itself, using the element order the probe pins (A: lane l
284	holds row l%16, element e is column e; B: lane l holds column l%16,
285	element e is row e). No LDS, no barrier, and the plain path stays as the
286	fallback the probe selects. The MoE Q4 GEMM's 51% is the first customer;
287	the LLM's prefill graph runs at 9.8 TFLOP/s of useful work (P11), most of
288	it on these kernels.

290	## Decisions (so future sessions don't relitigate)
291	
292	1. **The ceiling is per clock, and the clock is set by energy.** A
293	   kernel's utilisation is FLOP/clk/CU against the probe's 480, at the
294	   clock sysmon saw *during that kernel*. Every timing this vertical
295	   records carries its sclk and package power (PPT), and every kernel
296	   table carries **GFLOP/J** (or GB/J) beside its rate. The package is
297	   capped near 150 W (§0.6), so rate = cap ÷ energy per operation: a
298	   kernel that spends fewer joules a FLOP runs at a higher clock and is
299	   faster for that reason alone. Power efficiency is not a second
300	   objective here; it is the same one (§0.7).
301	2. **The suite is the ablation instrument; the vertical kernels are where
302	   a winner ships.** `gemm_wmma.comp` + `results/gemm_wmma.csv` stay a
303	   measured artifact of a kernel that does not move under them (the
304	   header in `dit_gemm.comp` says why). A lever is proved in the suite on
305	   the `shapes` family (the models' real M, N, K), then ported to
306	   `dit_gemm.comp` as a `-D` and screened in the verticals with their own
307	   tools: `TestGPUShapes`/`H3_PROFILE` (video), the zimage DiT ladder
308	   (image), `cmd/kevload`, the LLM prefill bench.
309	3. **Bit-identical or the vertical's own gate.** A scheduling change
310	   (prefetch, tile order, epilogue store) makes the same MMAs in the same
311	   order and must be byte-identical (`TestGPUForward` asserts it, as
312	   M11d's split did). A numeric change (lazy rescale, fp16 C) goes through
313	   the consumer's gate (rms ≤ 1.1e-4 on a context; the teacher-forced step
314	   bounds), never a max-abs on a free run.
315	4. **Read the ISA before building the arm.** `cmd/probe` is back; a
316	   hypothesis about scheduling or issue is checked in the disassembly
317	   first, because §2.3 and §6.1 showed that is where the answers were.
318	5. **Wave size and element order are per kernel, probed, with a plain
319	   fallback.** Nothing written against a lane layout ships without
320	   `checkCoopMatLayout`'s equivalent selecting it at first use.
321	6. **A finding is filed under the next free `§N.M`** (§2.9 the prefetch,
322	   §3.8 the attention rescale, §2.10 the register dequant …) with its
323	   file in `research/`, and the G-stage here points at it. Numbers are
324	   never reused.
325	7. **Stop when three consecutive well-formed hypotheses move nothing by
326	   2%.** The exit is a measured plateau, not a percentage: 85% is the
327	   target, not the gate.

415	### G1 — the shipped GEMM's schedule (2026-09-29)
416	
417	Filed as **§6.5** in `research/6.5-gemm-schedule.md`.
418	
419	**The loop, from the disassembly** (`dit_gemm_wg128x256_bt16_swz8`,
420	wave64, 240 VGPRs, no spill, no LDS; ACO says 6 subgroups a SIMD, which
421	is not the arithmetic of a 1536-register file at wave64 and is not
422	relied on). One iteration is one 16-wide K tile:
423	
424	| instructions | count | what |
425	|---|---|---|
426	| `v_wmma_f32_16x16x16_f16` | 32 | the 4×8 accumulator grid |
427	| `buffer_load_b128` | 24 | 4 A + 8 B fragments, 2 loads each, in 3 clauses |
428	| `s_add/s_mul/s_lshr/s_lshl/s_load/s_mov` | 56 | the B tile addresses, **recomputed every iteration** |
429	| `v_lshlrev/v_add3/v_mul_lo/v_mbcnt/v_and` | 29 | the A addresses and lane offset, likewise |
430	| `s_delay_alu` | 20 | dependency stalls in that arithmetic |
431	| `s_waitcnt` | 9 | `vmcnt(14)`, then 12, 10, … 0, four MMAs between each |
432	| `s_clause`, branch, compare | 5 | |
433	
434	Order: address arithmetic → all 24 loads → `s_waitcnt vmcnt(14)` (A and
435	the first B landed) → 4 MMAs → wait → 4 MMAs … → `vmcnt(0)` → the last 4
436	→ loop. **G-o3 answered: no.** ACO does not hoist the next tile's loads
437	above this tile's MMAs; each iteration pays the load latency once, from
438	the address arithmetic to the tenth load landing, with only the other
439	waves on the SIMD to fill it. 4.5 non-MMA instructions an MMA, so it is
440	not issue-bound by count (H3); but ~85 of them sit on the critical path
441	in front of the loads.
442	
443	**Occupancy does not move it** (`-DLDS_PAD`, an unused shared array that
444	caps workgroups a WGP; `H3_GEMM_SPV`, 480p, int8):
445	
446	| build | LDS | workgroups a CU | gemm qkv | gate / up | o | forward |
447	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
448	| shipped | 0 | ≥ 3 | 36.9 | 36.6 / 36.6 | 34.5 | 30.10 s |
449	| `LDS_PAD=4096` | 16 KB | 4 | 37.2 | 36.7 / 36.6 | 34.1 | 30.21 s |
450	| `LDS_PAD=8192` | 32 KB | 2 | 37.3 | 36.6 / 36.5 | 34.2 | 30.04 s |
451	| `LDS_PAD=16384` | 64 KB | **1** | 37.6 | 37.0 / 36.9 | 34.7 | 30.00 s |
452	
453	Flat to 1%, down to one 4-wave workgroup a CU. So the exposed latency is
454	not being covered by other waves at *any* of these occupancies, and
455	adding waves is not a lever (G-o2 is moot for this kernel).
456	
457	**Take the memory system away** (`-DL0_LOADS=1`: every fragment load
458	reads one of two K tiles, so the 24 loads are issued and waited for as
459	before but every one is an L0 hit; the result is garbage by
460	construction; the `down` projection keeps the shipped KRANGE build, so
461	it is a control):
462	
463	| | shipped, real loads | `L0_LOADS` | |
464	|---|---|---|---|
465	| gemm qkv | 36.9 | **43.6** | 1.18x |
466	| gemm gate / up | 36.6 / 36.6 | **44.2 / 44.0** | 1.21x |
467	| gemm o | 34.5 | **42.8** | 1.24x |
468	| gemm down (control, real loads) | 26.7 | 29.9 | the clock |
469	| attention (unchanged kernel) | 37.2 | 39.4 | the clock |
470	| sclk during the forward | 2600–2650 | 2650–2700 (less memory power) | |
471	| **per clock, FLOP/clk/CU** | **353 (74%)** | **~405 (82–85%)** | |
472	
473	So the gap decomposes: **~10 points are the memory system** (the
474	difference between L0 hits and the real slabs, at the same schedule),
475	and **~16 points are the in-wave schedule** with the loads perfect: the
476	once-a-tile stall from the address arithmetic through the L0 latency to
477	the tenth load, against ~1,090 clocks of MMA. Neither part responds to
478	occupancy, which is what the LDS arms say.
479	
480	**What G2 builds, in order** (re-ranked by the energy roofline, §0.7).
481	(1) Strength-reduce the addresses: every fragment's offset advances by a
482	constant per iteration, so the 85 instructions are 12 adds; cheap,
483	bit-identical, shortens the critical path in front of every iteration's
484	loads, and issue costs watts (the 4-chain probe burns 14 W more than the
485	16-chain one for the same MMAs). (2) Fewer bytes a FLOP: LDS sharing of
486	each slab across the workgroup's 4 waves (the two waves that share an A
487	slab each load it today; H6, untested at this tiling) and the largest
488	per-wave tile the registers allow, measured in TFLOP/s *and* W, because
489	traffic is the power and the power is the clock. (3) Prefetch one K
490	tile ahead into a second register set, so the loads a wave waits on
491	were issued 1,090 clocks earlier: +24 VGPRs, which at WN = 8 means a 4×4
492	or 8×4 grid instead; it buys the in-wave stall and no clock. Bit-identical
493	C for all three, `TestGPUForward`; every arm reports GFLOP/J.
494	
495	**Hypotheses after G0/G1:** H1 confirmed and larger than thought (10%
496	of the ceiling is the clock; G7 asks whether anything can be done about
497	it). H2 alive as the in-wave stall, not as an occupancy story. H3 alive
498	only as the address arithmetic on the critical path. H4, H5 unmeasured.
499	H6 is the ~10 memory points. H7 dead.
500	
501	### G2 — the prefetch that fits (2026-09-29)
502	
503	Filed as **§2.9** in `research/2.9-lds-staged-wave32-gemm.md`, with the
504	whole ladder. The shipped build is now `dit_gemm_wg128x256_lds_w32` (and
505	`_krange`): eight wave32 waves of 4×4 tiles in the same 128×256
506	workgroup, the K slab (two tiles) fetched by the workgroup as 6 `uvec4`
507	a lane a slab ahead, written to the other of two LDS planes behind the
508	MMAs, one barrier a slab, fragments read from LDS at a conflict-free
509	pitch of 36 halves. Bit-identical to the wave64 build (`H3_GEMM_REF`,
510	`TestGPUForward`).
511	
512	| 480p, int8 | qkv | gate / up | o | down | forward | sclk | per clock |
513	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
514	| wave64 4×8 (was shipped) | 37.2 | 37.3 / 37.1 | 35.4 | 28.7 | 29.86 s | 2620 | 74% |
515	| **`lds_w32`, two runs** | **41.1 / 40.9** | **40.7 / 40.7** | **38.9 / 39.1** | **40.8 / 40.6** | **27.16 / 27.11 s** | 2665 | **80%** |
516	
517	The three findings that decided it: **a wave64 fragment is 8 VGPRs**
518	(4x replicated across the lane groups), so §6.5's "+24 VGPRs" for a
519	prefetched tile was +96 and no register prefetch fits beside a 4×8
520	grid; **ACO copies a fragment carried across a loop back-edge element
521	by element** (200 `v_mov_b16` a trip), so the two register-pipelining
522	arms were dead before they ran, and only a build that carries nothing
523	(a hoisted two-tile slab: +18% at the same intensity; or LDS) measures
524	the idea; and **wave32 and LDS are one lever**: wave32 halves the bytes a
525	fragment read moves but caps the tile at 4×4 and, fed from global memory,
526	runs at 21.5; fed from LDS it runs at 40.9. Refused on the way, all
527	bit-identical: strength-reduced addresses (nothing: the arithmetic was
528	never the cost), four hoisted tiles (no better than two), the read
529	order inside a slab (nothing), LDS pitches of 16 and 24 halves (the
530	reads are `ds_load_b64`, 16 lanes a clock: 4-way and 2-way conflicted).
531	
532	**What is left** (§2.9 item 5): with the staging loads all L0 hits the
533	build reaches 82% per clock, so the global side is ~3 points and the
534	LDS-side schedule (64 `ds_load_b64`, 6 stores, a barrier and the
535	`lgkmcnt` ladder a 544-clock slab) is ~18. G-o8.
536	
537	### G8 — the carry-in (2026-09-29)
538	
539	Every host of the 128×256 kernel now creates `dit_gemm_wg128x256_lds_w32`
540	pinned to wave32 (a `wave` field on each variant table; `K % 32` where a
541	host checks its tiles), through its own gate and screen, the same
542	session, the machine otherwise idle:
543	
544	| host | gate | screen, old → new | note |
545	|---|---|---|---|
546	| `h3/dit` | `TestGPUForward`, bit-identical | 480p forward 29.86 → 27.11 s | G2 |
547	| `h3/vae` | `TestGPUDecoder`, PSNR 81.7 dB unchanged | 480p decode 37.1 → **35.5 s** device, 768p 66.1 s | its bias column made K = H + 16; K now rounds to the big GEMM's tile (`gemmVariants[gemmBig].bk`), the pad columns zero in A and B |
548	| `qimage/dit` | `TestGPUOracle1024` | `TestGPUGEMMScreen`, one staging: swz8 2179 → **`lds_w32` 2058 ms a step** (−5.6%; swz2/4/16 +30/+18/+10%) | the fifth arm of the screen, the default |
549	| `ace/dit` | `TestGPUDiT` | 8 forwards at 30 s / 2 / 4 / 10 min: **wave64 0.96** / lds 3.27 (w64 3.24) / **6.76** (6.93) / **18.79** (19.37) s | **the LDS build loses at 375 rows** (130 against 120 ms: 30 workgroups, the barrier shows), ties at 1500, wins 2.5–3% from 3000; `bigW64Rows = 1024` picks the wave64 build below that; the 64×64 rung is 131 / 488 / 1002 / 3215 ms, never the answer |
550	| `kev` (fp16 bank) | `TestGPURowMatchesKev` | `TestGPUGEMMLadder`, 494 tokens: 154.2 → **132.4 ms** (reg64 at 37 tokens 49.7 both days, so the machine is the same) | serves int8 (`q8m4`, 155.3 at 494), which the fp16 rung now beats there: G5's argument |
551	| `parakeet` | `TestGPUEncoderStack` | ladder, `wg128x256`: 138 / 384 / 768 / 1024 frames 28.8 / 36.9 / 67.3 / 111.6 → 31.1 / 40.9 / 66.9 / 109.1 ms | its plan never picks the rung (`reg32x32_w32` wins every clip); at 8–12 workgroups the build loses 8–11% |
552	| `zimage/qwen` | `TestGPUEncoder`, `TestGPUKernelsAgree` | — (its rung is the >192-token one) | rung name now `wg128x256_lds_w32` |
553	| `ocr` | `TestLM`, `TestEngine` (all six cases token-identical) | the page's 1,234-row prefill 100 → 102 ms | the prefill is 2.5% of a page |
554	| `ace/lm` | `TestLogits`, `TestDeterministic` | prefill 239 rows 106 ms | rows ≤ 256 are GEMVs |
555	
556	**The rule it adds:** the LDS-staged build needs the machine full. Its
557	per-slab barrier and staging cost show whenever the grid is under ~40
558	workgroups (rows × N / 32,768), and the hosts whose inputs are short
559	(parakeet, the LM prefills, a 30 s clip) already run smaller rungs or a
560	wave64 build there. Where a host's screen gave a number, it is above.
561	
562	## How to run
563	
564	- The suite: `go run ./cmd/bench -h`; families `peak`, `gemm_wmma`,
565	  `shapes`, `stride`, `moe`, `bank`. Results append to `results/*.csv`
566	  with sclk and power columns; the harness warms the clock to 97% first
567	  (§0.2).
568	- The ISA: `RADV_DEBUG=shaderstats go run ./cmd/probe shaders/X.spv [32|64]`
569	  and `RADV_DEBUG=asm …` (`MESA_SHADER_CACHE_DISABLE=1` for a repeat).
570	  Builds are `go generate ./shaders` lines in `shaders/shaders.go`; `.spv`
571	  is gitignored.
572	- A GEMM build from disk through H3: `H3_GEMM_SPV=path` (`H3_GEMM_WAVE=32`
573	  to pin the wave, `H3_GEMM_KRANGE_SPV=path` for the split down
574	  projection's companion), `H3_GEMM_REF=file` the bit-identical gate
575	  (written by the first run, compared by every later one); a loaded
576	  build that is wrong by construction (`L0_LOADS`, `STAGE_L0`) is still
577	  timed. The clock and power beside it: a 100 ms loop over
578	  `hwmon/freq1_input` and `power1_average` (G7 will fold it into
579	  `bench/sysmon.go`).
580	- The vertical screens: VIDEO.md M7/M11c/M11h (`H3_SHAPES=480 H3_PROFILE=1
581	  H3_BANK=q8`, `H3_ATTN_SPV`, `H3_CHUNK`), the image DiT's ladder in
582	  `research/stage-4-dit-graph.md`, Kev's `cmd/kevload`, the LLM's
583	  `cmd/llm -bench` (memory: it needs `LLM_BANK_CACHE`).
584	- Never edit a shader during a sweep; build the test binary to the
585	  scratchpad first, and check `ps` for another device run.
586	- Driver pinned in the record: Mesa 26.2.2 (RADV), glslc 2026.3, Vulkan
587	  1.4.354, kernel 7.1.8. A driver upgrade re-runs G0.
588	
589	## Open questions
590	
591	- ~~**G-o1.** Is 478 FLOP/clk/CU the hardware's dense WMMA rate or the
592	  probe's?~~ **The hardware's** (G0): 478–482 at 4/8/16 chains and at
593	  wave32, 15/16 of the spec's 512.
594	- ~~**G-o2.** Does RADV place a 4-wave workgroup across the WGP's four
595	  SIMDs or the CU's two?~~ **Moot for this kernel** (G1): its rate is
596	  flat from ≥ 3 workgroups a CU down to 1. ACO's "6 subgroups a SIMD" at
597	  240 wave64 VGPRs is still unexplained and still not relied on.
598	- ~~**G-o3.** Does ACO already hoist the next tile's fragment loads above
599	  the current tile's MMAs?~~ **No** (G1): the loop is address math, 24
600	  loads, a waitcnt ladder, 32 MMAs, branch.
601	- ~~**G-o5.** Which cache is the ~10 memory points (G1)? Latency (then G2's
602	  prefetch takes it) or L2/MALL bandwidth (then only traffic per FLOP
603	  does)?~~ **Latency, mostly** (G2): with the slab fetched a slab ahead
604	  the memory side is ~3 points (`STAGE_L0` control), and the down
605	  projection's MALL overflow went with it because the slab is read once
606	  a workgroup.
607	- **G-o8.** The LDS-side schedule is the remaining ~18 points of
608	  `lds_w32` (§2.9): a 544-clock slab carries 64 `ds_load_b64`, 6
609	  `ds_store`, a barrier and a `lgkmcnt` ladder whose first MMA waits for
610	  20 reads. Which of those is it? Candidates: the barrier's lockstep
611	  (every wave issues 64 reads at once after it), the LDS's rate for
612	  replicated 16-lane reads (2x at wave32), and a `ds_load_b128` the
613	  lowering never emits. A build that reads fragments from LDS without a
614	  barrier (single wave a workgroup) prices the barrier; the peak
615	  family's `bandwidth` at an LDS-resident size prices the reads.
616	- **G-o7.** What does a byte cost at L0, L1 and L2? DRAM is ~490 pJ and
617	  the MALL ~100 (§0.7); the GEMM's 1.3 TB/s of fragment traffic lives in
618	  the levels below, and their price decides whether LDS sharing (which
619	  moves bytes from L1 to LDS reads) is a saving or a wash. G0b.
620	- **G-o6.** The package budget is ~150 W and the CPU takes from it (G0:
621	  32 threads halve the GPU clock). What does the server's actual CPU
622	  work beside a device job cost (the audio decode's 32 threads, staging
623	  on 32 cores, tokenising), and is a lower thread cap or a lower CPU
624	  power limit a net win for the device? G7.
625	- **G-o4.** What is wave64's accumulator element order? The probe reads
626	  it; if it is the wave32 order with rows split across lane halves the
627	  transposed attention has a wave64 build for free (G4).
628	
629	## Handoff
630	
631	**2026-09-29, session 4: G8 carried to every host.** All nine hosts run
632	`dit_gemm_wg128x256_lds_w32` pinned to wave32, every gate passing (table
633	in G8): image step −5.6%, VAE decode −4.3%, Kev's fp16 pass 1.16x at 494
634	tokens; the build loses below ~1000 rows, so `ace/dit` keeps the wave64
635	build up to `bigW64Rows` (1024), and the VAE's bias-padded K rounds to
636	32. Also added: `ACE_DIT_BIG=w64|small` on `TestGPUStepTiming`; the
637	served binary still needs a redeploy. **Next:** G-o8 (the LDS-side 18
638	points), or G4 (attention), or G5 (int8 in registers: Kev's fp16 rung
639	now beats its int8 one at 494 tokens, which says the int8 kernels are
640	where the LDS round trip still costs).
641	
642	**2026-09-29, session 3: G2 done and shipped for H3.** The prefetch is
643	LDS at wave32, not registers: `dit_gemm_wg128x256_lds_w32` (+ `_krange`)
644	is bit-identical to the wave64 build and takes H3's projections 37 → 41
645	TFLOP/s, the split down projection 29 → 41 and a 480p forward 29.9 →
646	27.1 s (two runs, 0.2%), 74 → 80% per clock; `research/2.9-…` has the
647	twelve-rung ladder. Three facts for anyone touching the GEMM next: a
648	wave64 fragment is 8 VGPRs (4x replicated), ACO cannot carry a fragment
649	across a loop back-edge without copying it element by element (so
650	register pipelining of coopmat operands is dead on Mesa 26.2.2), and
651	LDS fragment reads are `ds_load_b64` (pitch 36 halves). Tools: `SR`,
652	`PIPE`, `DB`, `LDS_STAGE` (`A_LPITCH`/`B_LPITCH`, `BK_TILES` 1–2),
653	`STAGE_L0`, `LOAD_ORDER` in `dit_gemm.comp`; `H3_GEMM_WAVE`,
654	`H3_GEMM_KRANGE_SPV`, `H3_GEMM_REF` in `TestGPUShapes`; a `wave` field
655	on H3's GEMM variant table. **Next:** G8 for the eight other hosts of
656	the 128×256 kernel (pin wave32, K % 32, each vertical's screen; the
657	image DiT's `dit.qkv` at M = 4096 is the number the record quotes), then
658	G-o8 or G4 (attention, whose head-128 builds spill 112–126 and whose
659	fragments are the same 8 VGPRs). The suite (`gemm_wmma.comp`) was not
660	ported; the lever was proved on H3's shapes with the bit-identical gate
661	and the clock instead, which G2's gate asked for in the other order.
662	
663	**2026-09-29, session 2: G0 and G1 done.** The ceiling is the hardware's
664	(480 FLOP/clk/CU, flat across chains and wave size). **The clock under a
665	real kernel is 2600–2650 MHz at ~149 W**, so a video forward's ceiling is
666	49.9 TFLOP/s and the shipped GEMM is at 74% of it, the attention 75%;
667	32 busy CPU threads halve the clock (a forward 1.67x slower), which is
668	M11f's mechanism. The GEMM's loop has no cross-tile prefetch and
669	recomputes 85 address instructions an iteration; its rate is flat from
670	1 to 3+ workgroups a CU; with every load an L0 hit it reaches 82–85%
671	per clock. So: ~10 points memory, ~16 points in-wave schedule. **Next is
672	G2** in the order above: strength-reduced addresses, then a one-tile
673	register prefetch, screened with `H3_GEMM_SPV` at 480p and in the suite,
674	bit-identical via `TestGPUForward`. Tools added: `cmd/probe` (restored),
675	`-DWAVE`/`-DACC` peak variants, `-DLDS_PAD` and `-DL0_LOADS` screening
676	knobs in `dit_gemm.comp` (never shipped builds), `H3_GEMM_SPV`. The
677	scratchpad sampler is not in the tree (G7).
678	
679	**2026-09-29, session 1: the vertical reopened.** Record assembled from
680	`research/ideas.md`, `stage-4-dit-graph.md`, `stage-3-dit-attention.md`,
681	VIDEO.md M11c–M11h and `results/*.csv`. New facts today: the suite's
682	best GEMM ran at **2813 MHz and 137 W** where the peak probe ran at 2899
683	and 110, so the per-clock utilisation is 72.6% (39.0) and 76–78% (42.0,
684	clock unrecorded); the shipped GEMM is **240 VGPRs, no spill, no LDS,
685	`BK_TILES 1`, no hoist**; both shipped head-128 attentions spill 112–126
686	VGPRs; `cmd/probe` was deleted on 2026-09-22 by accident and is
687	**restored** (`cmd/probe/main.go`, from `501053a^`). Outside numbers:
688	36.9 TFLOP/s is the best public figure on this chip, 92% of peak is what
689	rocBLAS reaches on a 7900 XTX. Nothing else built. Next: G0, then G1.
690

# KERNELS — the matrix cores to their ceiling

> **Live tracking and session handoff doc, opened 2026-09-29.** Stage
> letters are **G** (GEMM; K is classification, W and R are speech). This
> is the project's first vertical, reopened: not a model, but the kernels
> every vertical stands on. A closed finding still gets a `§N.M` number and
> a file in `research/` as before (README there: the number is the address,
> never renumber); the G-stage here is where it is tracked while open. When
> the vertical closes, this file is frozen to `research/kernels-vertical.md`.

## What we are building

`GOALS.md`'s first sentence: *the most efficient ways to run these models
on Vulkan on this part*. Every vertical since has been a model brought up
on the kernels this one produced, and each of them ended on the same
sentence: "the GEMMs are at their ceiling, the bigger fish is elsewhere".
That ceiling was **42.0 TFLOP/s against a measured 55.5**, and it has not
moved since stage 4 (2026-09-21). Eight verticals later, the matrix cores
are the one place where a win lands in *every* served request at once: a
480p video forward is 63% GEMM and 33% attention on these kernels, an
image step 72% GEMM, a prefill chunk mostly GEMM. **A 1.15x on the GEMM is
worth more than any single vertical's remaining backlog.**

The deliverable is three kernel classes at a higher fraction of the
per-clock ceiling than today, carried into the verticals through the
screens they already have, and the ceiling itself pinned better than it
is:

| class | file | today | target |
|---|---|---|---|
| fp16 WMMA GEMM (activation × fp16 weight) | `shaders/dit_gemm.comp` (the vertical kernel), `shaders/gemm_wmma.comp` (the ablation suite) | 39.0 suite / **42.0** pipeline, 72–78% | ≥ 85% per clock |
| WMMA flash attention | `shaders/h3_attn_t.comp` (transposed, wave32), `shaders/dit_attention_wmma.comp` (plain) | **37.6–38.8**, 68–70% | ≥ 80% |
| int8 / Q4-weight WMMA GEMM | `shaders/llm_moe_gemm.comp`, `shaders/llm_gemm.comp`, `shaders/kev_gemm_q8_glu.comp`, `dit_dequant_q8` + fp16 GEMM (video) | 51% (MoE Q4, §2.2), the rest unmeasured against the ceiling | the fp16 GEMM's rate at the same M, N, K |
| streaming kernels (norms, packs, gates, SwiGLU, copies) | everywhere | 6–14% of every block; `hc.cn` at 134 GB/s (TODO) | ≥ 200 GB/s each, or fused away |

Decode is not in the table: §1.7–§1.12 took the GEMV to 96–103% of the
bus, and the LLM's decode has been a *format* question since (L8).

## What we did (the record, so it is not re-run)

The kernel work of 2026-09-13 to 09-21 is filed under `§N.M` in
`research/ideas.md` and its per-item files. The ladder, on the fp16 GEMM:

| step | lever | best GEMM | of 55.5 | file |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| §0 | the ceilings measured on this chip, not extrapolated | — | — | `0-measurement-validity.md` |
| baseline | one 16×16 accumulator a wave, `gemm_coopmat_fp16.comp` | 4.9 | 9% | |
| §2.1 | register blocking: a WM×WN accumulator grid a wave (AI 8 → 32) | 25.2 | 45% | `2.1-register-blocking.md` |
| §2.3 | padded leading dimensions: a K-strided fragment load off one DRAM channel | 28.4 | 51% | `2.3-channel-aliasing.md` |
| §2.7 | a whole K-slab's fragment loads in flight before its first MMA | 39.0 | 70% | `2.7-kslab-hoist.md` |
| §2.8 | the weight stored as 16×16 fragment tiles (packed once at upload) | 41.0 on two of three shapes | 74% | `stage-4-dit-graph.md` |
| §2.4 | the grid walked in bands of 8 columns (MALL locality) | **42.0 / 41.1 / 40.6** on the DiT's three shapes | 73–76% | `stage-4-dit-graph.md` |

And on the others:

- **Attention** (§3.3, `stage-3-dit-attention.md`): both matmuls on the
  matrix cores, online softmax, every operand as fragment tiles: 1.28 →
  **38.8 TFLOP/s** (30x), wave32 a clean 1.40x over wave64 at the same
  tiling. Then VIDEO.md **M11c**: the LDS round trip that turned P from an
  accumulator into an operand was ~60% of the kernel; computing S^T and
  O^T instead puts P^T on the B side with one shuffle per element pair, no
  LDS, no barrier, 1.55–1.61x on H3's kernel. M11e carried it to head 64.
- **Q4 weights on the matrix cores** (§2.2): 2.10x a MoE block, at **51%**
  of the matrix cores, because the operand must round-trip through LDS
  ("no extension exposes a fragment's lane layout"). **That premise is now
  false**: M11c's `coopmat_layout_probe.comp` reads the element order back
  and it is fixed and simple on this device.
- **Grouped MoE GEMM** (§3.5): 1.1–4.1x, and the mechanism was occupancy.
- **conv2d as an implicit GEMM** (stage 8): conv3x3 at **41–42 TFLOP/s**;
  the dilated 1-D convolutions of kokoro's vocoder on `dit_gemm`'s
  `A_CONV` at 22.4.
- **Decode GEMV** (§1.1, §1.7–§1.12): 96–103% of the 236 GB/s bus at
  every N; done.
- **Wave size** (§6.2): a per-pipeline knob; the GEMM spills at wave32 and
  loses, the fragment-dominated kernels gain 1.4–2.1x.
- **The ISA** (§6.1): `cmd/probe` + `RADV_DEBUG=asm|shaderstats`. It found
  §2.3 (a row-major B fragment is sixteen scalar loads). **It was deleted
  by accident on 2026-09-22** (collateral in a speech commit, README still
  documented it) and **restored today**.

**Refused, measured, so not to be re-run without a new reason:** LDS
staging of A/B slabs (§2.1, lost at every tile; the MALL supplies the
reuse), LDS double-buffering (same), split-K on the big shapes (M11d: two K
passes buy 1.02x on `down` only because its A chunk overflows the MALL,
and a chunk of 4096 gets the same without it), swizzle bands other than 8
(§2.4, M11d), A row pads other than 128 (M11d), QT4 and KTIL8 attention
builds (spill), the lane-split row max (P12-1, slower everywhere), wave32
for the register-blocked GEMM (spills, −25%), an int8 *kernel* where the
GEMM is compute-bound (WMMA int8 runs at the fp16 rate, §0.1).

attentions spill more than 100 registers to scratch.

## The energy roofline (2026-09-29, §0.7)

The GEMM ladder at N = 2048 drew **136–137 W at every rung from 23 to 39
TFLOP/s**; the winner won by needing less energy a FLOP under the same
cap. So the roofline that binds a real kernel on this part is joules,
not clocks, and it is already in `results/*.csv` (the `power_w` column):

| what | rate | PPT | energy | above ~20 W idle |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| matrix pipe, registers only, 16 chains (`peak`) | 55.5 TFLOP/s | 98 W | **567 GFLOP/J** | 1.4 pJ a FLOP |
| the same at 4 chains (the old probe) | 55.5 | 112 W | 495 | +14 W of loop issue |
| `dot4_int8` / packed fp16 FMA / fp32 FMA | 54 / 25 / 23 T | 118–121 W | 450 / 215 / 189 | |
| MALL-resident copy (1–4 MB) | 800 GB/s | 105–136 W | 6–8 GB/J | ~100 pJ a byte |
| DRAM stream (≥ 6 MB) | 236 GB/s | 136 W | **1.7 GB/J** | **~490 pJ a byte** |
| best suite GEMM | 39.0 TFLOP/s | 137 W | 285 GFLOP/J | |
| a video forward, every kernel | 32.5 TFLOP/s | 149 W | 218 GFLOP/J | |
| LLM prefill, 8,192 tokens, 24 of 48 layers (`cmd/llm -graph`) | 2,680 tok/s (≈1,340 at 48) | **142 W** at 2713 MHz | ≈ 110 mJ a token at 48 layers | |
| LLM decode, 24 of 48 layers (`cmd/llm -gen`) | 63.2 tok/s (≈31.6 at 48) | **91 W** at 2590 MHz | ≈ 2.9 J a token at 48 layers | memory-bound: the bytes, not the clock |

A DRAM byte costs the energy of ~340 matrix FLOPs, a MALL byte ~70.
The matrix cores at full rate are ~80 W over idle, so **at a 150 W cap a
real GEMM has ~50 W for everything else** (bytes at every level, address
arithmetic, issue), which is 100 GB/s of DRAM-priced traffic or ~500 GB/s
of MALL-priced: a kernel at 55 TFLOP/s and AI 43 moves 1.3 TB/s through
the L0/L1, and whether that fits depends on the pJ a byte at *those*
levels, which are not measured (G0b). This is also why a
register-resident loop "reaches peak at ~90 W" wherever it is claimed:
that is the probe, and the other 50–70 W in a real kernel is bytes.

**An outside calibration** (2026-09-29): `peonist-ai/halogen-flash-server`
claims, for the same model on the same part, prefill at 1,567–1,584 tok/s
(8k–32k prompts) and 1,517 at 131k, serial decode 37.6 tok/s at 1.5k and
34.1 at 32k, and 46–56 tok/s with a draft head plus prompt lookup, at
"about 85 W of sustained package power" and a 2,229 MHz median clock
during a 32k prefill. Against ours: prefill 1,213 at 8k and 1,011–1,022
at 128k (1.25–1.5x behind) at 142 W (so ~2x the energy a token); serial
decode 34.4 at depth 0 and 31.5 at 128k (within 10%) at 91 W (about
the same joules a token as their 108–118 W would give); our speculative
loop is parked at 0.95x where theirs is 1.35–1.5x. The repository is
documentation and a container image, not source ("Shell", no kernel
files), so the how is not inspectable. The image was not run here, on
purpose: the hardware is the same part under the same ~150 W cap, so
their 85 W at 2229 MHz is what their prefill *draws*, not a limit it
runs under, and the comparison needs no more than the two power
readings. The prefill gap is the one this vertical can act on: a 2x in
joules a token at a *lower* clock says their prefill moves far fewer
bytes a token through the memory system than ours, which is G5's
territory (4-bit weights straight into the matrix cores without the LDS
round trip) and G6's (the streaming kernels between the GEMMs).

What it changes: an arm that hides latency without moving fewer bytes
(a register prefetch) buys the in-wave stall and no clock; an arm that
moves fewer bytes a FLOP (LDS sharing across a workgroup's waves, bigger
effective tiles, fewer wasted instructions) buys twice. G2's order below
is set by that.

## Why 76% and not 90%: the hypotheses, each with its measurement

Every GEMM lever in the tree so far changed *what* is loaded (intensity,
stride, layout, order). None changed *when*, except §2.7, which changed only
the scheduling and was worth 2.1x. The remaining gap is most likely
scheduling again.

- **H1 — the clock.** 3% is already measured (2813 against 2899). Whether
  a sustained kernel loses more is §6.4, never run. *Measure*: sysmon over
  a 60 s GEMM loop and over one H3 forward, CPU idle and CPU busy (the
  server tokenises and decodes audio beside the device). Cheap, and it
  fixes the denominator for everything below.
- **H2 — latency exposed at the K-tile boundary.** The shipped loop is
  `BK_TILES 1`, no hoist: per K tile a wave issues 4 A + 8 B fragment loads
  and 32 MMAs, then the next tile's loads. 32 wave64 MMAs are ~1,100 clocks
  of matrix-pipe time (8,192 FLOP each at 239 FLOP/clk/SIMD); a fragment
  load from L2 or the MALL is several hundred to ~2,000 clocks. Unless the
  compiler already issues tile k+1's loads before tile k's MMAs, each wave
  stalls once a tile, and with 2–3 waves a SIMD the pipe idles part of the
  time. A 20–25% shortfall is exactly the size of one exposed latency per
  tile at this occupancy. *Measure*: G1 reads the ISA (where the
  `s_waitcnt` sits relative to the `v_wmma` block), then G2 builds the
  register-prefetch arm: tile k+1's 12 fragments loaded into a second
  register set before tile k's MMAs issue. That is +24 VGPRs; at WN = 8 it
  is 264 and spills, so the arm is WM 4 × WN 4 (16 accumulators, 64 VGPRs)
  in a 4-wave 128×128 workgroup, or WM 8 × WN 4, and the AI drop (43 → 32)
  is part of what is measured. **This is the lever the plan is built
  around.** *G2's answer (§2.9): the latency is the cost, but a fragment
  is 8 VGPRs (4x replicated at wave64), ACO copies any fragment carried
  across the loop's back-edge element by element, and the prefetch that
  fits is a whole slab through LDS at wave32: 74 → 80% per clock.*
- **H3 — the issue budget.** A wave64 MMA holds the matrix pipe ~34 clocks;
  if the loop spends more than ~30 VALU/SALU issue slots per MMA on
  address arithmetic, waitcnts and loads, the SIMD is issue-bound, not
  latency-bound. *Measure*: instruction count per K tile from the ISA
  (§2.3's route: the B-layout finding was an instruction count). If it is
  under ~8 non-MMA instructions an MMA, this is not it.
- **H4 — the epilogue.** 32 fp32 tiles a wave stored row-major with no
  overlap inside the wave: 63 MB of C at M = 4096 × N = 3840, 0.27 ms at
  the bus, of a 2.9 ms GEMM. **~9% if nothing overlaps it**, and other
  workgroups' MMAs only overlap it if a second workgroup fits on the CU.
  *Measure*: the `C_F16` build (halves it; already exists, allowed where
  the consumer narrows anyway) against the fp32 store, and a control that
  stores one tile of the 32 (the compiler must not be allowed to drop the
  MMAs: keep the store conditional on a push constant).
- **H5 — the grid tail.** 480 workgroups of 128×256 at the DiT's shape, one
  or two resident a CU, so 6–12 rounds; a shape whose last round is a
  quarter full loses up to a round. *Measure*: rate against M in steps of
  128 rows on one N, K; the tail's size falls out of the sawtooth.
- **H6 — L0/L1 traffic.** At 42 TFLOP/s and AI 43 the fragment loads move
  ~1 TB/s, above the MALL's 965 GB/s pure read, so the L0/L1 hit rate is
  carrying the kernel. The two waves of a workgroup that share an A slab
  each load it. LDS staging lost in §2.1 at AI 8–32 on an unhoisted,
  untiled kernel; it has not been asked at the current tiling. *Measure*:
  only after G2, and only if the prefetch arm lands short of 85%: one LDS
  arm on the *tiled* B (a slab is 512 B contiguous tiles, so the staging
  is a copy, not a gather). *G2: built, and it is the shipped kernel;
  with the staging loads made L0 hits the build reaches 82%, so the memory
  system is now ~3 points and the LDS-side schedule ~18 (G-o8).*
- **H7 — the accumulator chain.** 32 independent accumulators a K tile;
  the MMA latency is hidden. Not it; listed so no one re-tests it.

**Attention** (68–70%, and both shipped head-128 builds spill 112–126):

- **A1 — the spill.** `T QT2 KTIL4` spills 112 and wins; `T QT2 KTIL2` is
  spill-free at 256 and loses 15%; reloading Q each block removes the
  spill and loses 11%. Untried: **a head-dimension split** (two passes of
  64 channels; the head-64 build is spill-free at 240 and runs 34
  TFLOP/s on the VAE), and **wave64** for the transposed kernel (its
  element order is wave32's; the probe says what wave64's is, and at wave64
  the same tile needs half the VGPRs per fragment). *Measure*: the existing
  screen (`TestGPUAttentionScreen`, `H3_ATTN_SPV=qt:ktil:path`).
- **A2 — the online rescale.** Every key block rescales the 8 O^T
  accumulator tiles of a query tile, 8 elements a lane each, plus the
  running sum, whether or not the row max moved. FlashAttention-3's lazy
  rescaling skips it while the max grows by less than a threshold and
  corrects once at the end; exact up to fp32 rounding order. *Measure*:
  the screen, and rms against the plain kernel ≤ 1.1e-4 as M11c gated.
- **A3 — an honest gutting.** M11c's "no LDS round trip" arm read 65.7
  TFLOP/s, above the ceiling, so the compiler dropped MMAs and that arm is
  not a measurement. *Redo*: each phase removed with its result kept live
  (folded into the stored O), so the MMA-only floor of the transposed loop
  is a real number. If it is ~40, the softmax is not the cost and A1 is
  the whole story; if 45+, A2 is worth up to 15%.

**Int8 and Q4 weights** (the LLM's prefill, Kev, embeddings, video's
dequant pass): **G5** builds the B fragment in registers from the bytes
the lane loads itself, using the element order the probe pins (A: lane l
holds row l%16, element e is column e; B: lane l holds column l%16,
element e is row e). No LDS, no barrier, and the plain path stays as the
fallback the probe selects. The MoE Q4 GEMM's 51% is the first customer;
the LLM's prefill graph runs at 9.8 TFLOP/s of useful work (P11), most of
it on these kernels.

## Decisions (so future sessions don't relitigate)

1. **The ceiling is per clock, and the clock is set by energy.** A
   kernel's utilisation is FLOP/clk/CU against the probe's 480, at the
   clock sysmon saw *during that kernel*. Every timing this vertical
   records carries its sclk and package power (PPT), and every kernel
   table carries **GFLOP/J** (or GB/J) beside its rate. The package is
   capped near 150 W (§0.6), so rate = cap ÷ energy per operation: a
   kernel that spends fewer joules a FLOP runs at a higher clock and is
   faster for that reason alone. Power efficiency is not a second
   objective here; it is the same one (§0.7).
2. **The suite is the ablation instrument; the vertical kernels are where
   a winner ships.** `gemm_wmma.comp` + `results/gemm_wmma.csv` stay a
   measured artifact of a kernel that does not move under them (the
   header in `dit_gemm.comp` says why). A lever is proved in the suite on
   the `shapes` family (the models' real M, N, K), then ported to
   `dit_gemm.comp` as a `-D` and screened in the verticals with their own
   tools: `TestGPUShapes`/`H3_PROFILE` (video), the zimage DiT ladder
   (image), `cmd/kevload`, the LLM prefill bench.
3. **Bit-identical or the vertical's own gate.** A scheduling change
   (prefetch, tile order, epilogue store) makes the same MMAs in the same
   order and must be byte-identical (`TestGPUForward` asserts it, as
   M11d's split did). A numeric change (lazy rescale, fp16 C) goes through
   the consumer's gate (rms ≤ 1.1e-4 on a context; the teacher-forced step
   bounds), never a max-abs on a free run.
4. **Read the ISA before building the arm.** `cmd/probe` is back; a
   hypothesis about scheduling or issue is checked in the disassembly
   first, because §2.3 and §6.1 showed that is where the answers were.
5. **Wave size and element order are per kernel, probed, with a plain
   fallback.** Nothing written against a lane layout ships without
   `checkCoopMatLayout`'s equivalent selecting it at first use.
6. **A finding is filed under the next free `§N.M`** (§2.9 the prefetch,
   §3.8 the attention rescale, §2.10 the register dequant …) with its
   file in `research/`, and the G-stage here points at it. Numbers are
   never reused.
7. **Stop when three consecutive well-formed hypotheses move nothing by
   2%.** The exit is a measured plateau, not a percentage: 85% is the
   target, not the gate.
